## LedgerTaxLotDisposalHistoryRecord

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.Ledger.LedgerTaxLotDisposalHistoryRecord</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerJournalStore.TaxLotDisposalHistory.cs:18](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerJournalStore.TaxLotDisposalHistory.cs#L18).

A retained disposal as durable history, without the two facts that live on the journal rather than in tax-lot storage: the sale&#x27;s effective date and the gain or loss actually booked. The caller supplies those from the journal entries it already holds, which keeps the rebuilt rows tied to the same journals a report pack was certified over. PolicyRevision is the exact revision recorded on the batch, never today&#x27;s account policy. RecordedAt is the atomic retention time, not proof that a later replacement window was re-evaluated or finalized.

## LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.Ledger.LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs:13](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs#L13).

The seam between the canonical FaceValueLot aggregate and the durable lot of record. FaceValueLot owns the par-denominated economics — cost basis, premium/discount, factor-restated face, amortized basis — and this is where those conventions are written onto LedgerTaxLotRecord and read back off it, so a persisted lot can be restated as the aggregate rather than re-derived by each consumer against a hardcoded 100.

```csharp
public static class LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms
```

| Declaration | Source | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>public const decimal LedgerLotParBasis = 100m;</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs:21](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs#L21) | The par basis the ledger engines&#x27; lot math assumes: price per 100 of par, quantity = face / 100. A lot&#x27;s own LedgerTaxLotRecord.ParBasis records the basis its price was originally struck in, which is what lets a per-unit quote survive persistence without silently mis-amortizing through math that assumes this one. |
| <code>public static LedgerTaxLotRecord WithFaceValueTerms(this LedgerTaxLotRecord record, FaceValueLot lot);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs:29](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs#L29) | Records lot&#x27;s acquisition-time par conventions on the lot of record. The aggregate and the record must already describe the same acquisition: the record&#x27;s quantity is the face expressed in the engines&#x27; unit convention, so it must equal the aggregate&#x27;s face over LedgerLotParBasis, and cost basis must tie under both readings. |
| <code>public static FaceValueLot? ToFaceValueLot(this LedgerTaxLotRecord record);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs:79](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/LedgerTaxLotFaceValueTerms.cs#L79) | Restates a persisted lot as the canonical aggregate, or returns null when the lot recorded no face terms — the lot of record carries them all-three-or-none, and a lot booked before they existed states nothing rather than defaulting to a price-per-100 quote at factor 1. Callers that need face economics must fail closed on the null rather than substituting a quantity. A lot that has absorbed a paydown rehydrates at the factor it currently holds, so its FaceValueLot.FaceOutstanding is the paid-down face; a lot still at its booked factor rehydrates there. |

## PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.Ledger.PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs:26](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs#L26).

Surveys and repairs the currency detail that historical journal legs are missing. V_ledger_026 added transaction currency, both transaction-side amounts, and the FX rate to journal_legs as nullable columns, and legs written before it have them null. So do legs written after it but before #2800, because the shared validator&#x27;s dimension rebuild dropped a line&#x27;s currency on the way to the store. The append path is fixed; nothing repairs what is already retained, and nothing reports it either — a currency-blind leg reads back as a leg that simply has no currency detail. The repair only ever writes the identity translation — transaction currency equal to the functional currency, transaction amounts equal to the functional amounts, FX rate 1 — and never touches a leg&#x27;s debit or credit. The original rate on a foreign leg is not recoverable from anything retained, so this deliberately refuses to invent one: see LedgerCurrencyBackfillDisposition for what each refusal means.

```csharp
public sealed class PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill
```

Declared public members:

| Declaration | Source | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>public PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill(LedgerJournalStoreOptions options);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs:30](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs#L30) |  |
| <code>public async Task&lt;LedgerCurrencyBackfillSurvey&gt; SurveyAsync(CancellationToken ct = default);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs:41](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs#L41) | Reports every retained leg still missing its currency detail, grouped by ledger book and by what can be done about it. This is the surface the gap shows up on: currency-blind legs are otherwise indistinguishable from legs that were never meant to carry currency. |
| <code>public async Task&lt;int&gt; RepairEvidencedLegsAsync(CancellationToken ct = default);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs:78](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs#L78) | Repairs every leg the retained evidence already determines, and returns how many were completed. V_ledger_029 runs the same repair once at migration time; this re-runs it, which matters because a book that had no currency evidence then accumulates it with every posting appended since — the same legs become repairable without anyone having to assert anything. |
| <code>public async Task&lt;LedgerCurrencyAffirmationResult&gt; AffirmSingleCurrencyBookAsync(Guid ledgerBookId, string currency, string actor, string rationale, CancellationToken ct = default);</code> | [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs:118](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerCurrencyBackfill.cs#L118) | Completes the currency-blind legs of one ledger book on an operator&#x27;s assertion that the book transacted only in currency, and records that assertion as the authority for the change. This is narrow on purpose. It completes an evidence gap; it never overrules evidence. A book whose legs show foreign-currency denomination, or whose functional currency disagrees with its base currency, is refused — no affirmation makes an unrecoverable FX rate recoverable. So is a book whose blind legs the data already determines, which needs RepairEvidencedLegsAsync and no assertion at all. |

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerJournalStore.AverageCostRelief.cs:14](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/PostgresLedgerJournalStore.AverageCostRelief.cs#L14).

Atomic average-cost relief. The disposal books the pooled basis the canonical guard certified, and every surviving lot in the pool is restated to the pooled basis in the same transaction, so the lots of record still tie to the asset account the journal credited. Restatements are governed basis adjustments: acquisition facts never change.

## RetainedPostingEquivalence

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.Ledger.RetainedPostingEquivalence</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/RetainedPostingEquivalence.cs:28](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/RetainedPostingEquivalence.cs#L28).

Compares a retained journal against the posting a caller is asking to append, so a posting-identity collision can be resolved as an exact replay rather than assumed to be one. The comparison is deliberately restricted to canonical economic content — lineage, period, policy, timing, idempotency, and the ordered lines. Generated identities are excluded because they are not stable across two builds of the same request: each build mints a fresh JournalEntry.JournalEntryId and fresh per-line entry ids, and the lineDimensions.&lt;entryId&gt;.* compatibility tags are keyed by those ids. Comparing them would report a conflict for a posting that is economically identical, which turns an ordinary operator retry into a hard failure. Approval-derived state is excluded for the same reason: approval id, approval state, the fingerprint computed over the approved command, and evidence retention stamps are all recorded at append time, so a later replay of the same posting legitimately carries different values. That exclusion is deliberately narrow — everything else a tag carries, including the real-versus-simulated provenance mark and the economic-event and projection lineage, is compared. What must not differ is what the books say, and what the figures claim to be.

## WashSaleDeferralRecord

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Storage.Ledger.WashSaleDeferralRecord</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/WashSaleDeferralRecord.cs:23](../../../../src/Meridian.Storage/Ledger/WashSaleDeferralRecord.cs#L23).

A retained wash-sale deferral: one loss-generating disposal capitalized DisallowedAmount into one replacement lot. Retention is what makes the deferral survive past the period it was computed in — a later sale of the replacement lot replays these rows as basis adjustments, so the deferred loss is finally recognized at the right time and with the carried holding period, instead of disappearing.

```csharp
public sealed record WashSaleDeferralRecord(Guid DeferralId, Guid LedgerBookId, Guid DisposalMutationBatchId, Guid SecurityId, DateOnly SaleDate, LedgerAccount DisposalAccount, Guid ReplacementTaxLotRecordId, string ReplacementLotId, decimal DisallowedAmount, decimal MatchedReplacementQuantity, DateOnly HoldingPeriodCarryDate, string PolicyId, int WindowDays, WashSaleReplacementScope Scope, DateTimeOffset RecordedAt);
```
